Testing magnetic semiconductor devices comes with a unique challenge: the magnetic field can interfere with the test itself. Hprobe develops dedicated magnetic testing solutions that combine controlled magnetic field generation with electrical testing, helping manufacturers characterize advanced magnetic devices accurately and repeatably at wafer level.
are increasingly used in automotive, industrial, consumer and other advanced applications.
. This creates additional requirements for semiconductor test equipment, particularly when manufacturers need to characterize devices accurately and repeatably at wafer level.

Its solutions are designed to help semiconductor manufacturers characterize magnetic devices under controlled conditions, from early-stage research and development through to advanced production environments.

These systems combine controlled magnetic stimulation with electrical measurements, allowing manufacturers and research organizations to study device behavior, switching characteristics and magnetic performance at wafer level.
Hprobe develops dedicated solutions to help researchers and semiconductor manufacturers investigate magnetic immunity in technologies such as STT-MRAM.

Hprobe’s magnetic sensor test solutions are designed to provide controlled magnetic stimulation at wafer level, helping manufacturers characterize sensor performance while maintaining repeatability across devices and wafers.
, the event brings together semiconductor manufacturers, equipment suppliers, researchers and technology companies working across the semiconductor ecosystem.

As MRAM and magnetic sensor technologies progress toward industrial manufacturing, test solutions must evolve with them. Equipment that works well for a small number of devices in an R&D environment may not necessarily meet the requirements of high-volume semiconductor manufacturing.
The objective is to provide manufacturers and research organizations with reliable magnetic test capabilities as magnetic technologies move from the laboratory toward commercial production.

Hprobe’s solutions support applications ranging from advanced R&D and device characterization to semiconductor manufacturing, helping customers address the specific challenges associated with magnetic device testing.
high-volume manufacturing

Spin-transfer torque magnetic random-access memory (STT-MRAM) is increasingly used for embedded and standalone non-volatile memory applications, including automotive, industrial, and edge-computing systems. Because STT-MRAM stores information in the magnetic state of a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ), an important reliability question is its sensitivity to external magnetic fields.

STT-MRAM stores data by switching the magnetization of a magnetic free layer between two stable states. During normal operation, the magnetic stability of this layer is designed to be high enough to prevent unwanted switching caused by external magnetic fields.

As MRAM moves into demanding applications such as automotive electronics, industrial systems and advanced embedded memory, understanding magnetic robustness becomes an important part of device qualification and technology development.
This approach allows semiconductor manufacturers, memory developers and research organizations to characterize magnetic immunity from device development through technology qualification.
, supporting the transition to high-volume manufacturing, and enhancing reliability and performance for end-users.
